scope: All twelve complete bo/dz position-control values compared to the exact English, independently parsed and checked at clause level. Primary sources checked anew where uncertain. No source/repository modifications.

entries.note: Exact/precise location is expressed by a complete noun-plus-modifier label. It does not mean only a location in this UI context.
Reads as the intended value of X, in pixels counted from the left edge. The relative clause modifies pixels; its origin is physical left, not logical start, and X remains the labelled coordinate.
Reads as the intended value of Y, in pixels counted from the upper edge. The corresponding label structure is coherent; top is physical rather than later draw order.

entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.
entries.target: པར་རིས་འདིའི་གཡོན་སྟེང་གི་ཟུར་དེ་གྲུབ་འབྲས་ཀྱི་རས་གཞིའི་ཐོག་གནས་འཇོག་བྱོས། X དང་ Y ནི་པིག་སེལ་གྱི་ཧྲིལ་གྲངས་ཡིན་ཞིང་ 0 ནས་འགོ་འཛུགས། པར་རིས་གཞན་རྣམས་རང་རང་གི་ད་ལྟའི་གནས་སུ་གནས། འདིར་པར་རིས་ཕན་ཚུན་བརྩེགས་ཆོག རྗེས་སུ་ནང་འཇུག་བྱས་པའི་པར་རིས་རྣམས་སྔོན་གྱི་པར་རིས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྟེང་དུ་འབྲི། གནས་བཞག་ཟིན་པའི་པར་རིས་ཚང་མ་ཤོང་བར་རས་གཞི་ཆེ་རུ་འགྱུར། གཅོད་ཁུལ་དང་ཆེ་ཆུང་རྣམས་མི་འགྱུར།
entries.note: All seven source units were read in order as a connected instruction. It places this image’s top-left corner, states integer-pixel coordinates beginning at 0, leaves other positions, allows overlap, renders later imports over earlier ones, grows the canvas to accommodate every placed image, and leaves both crop regions and sizes. The result-canvas and positioning compounds are somewhat literal but recoverable and not a meaning-changing defect.

entries.source: X and Y must be whole numbers from zero to 2147483647.
entries.target: X དང་ Y གཉིས་ཀ་ 0 ནས་ 2147483647 བར་གྱི་ཧྲིལ་གྲངས་ཡིན་དགོས།
entries.note: The dual subject is explicit; integer type, obligation and both exact endpoints are retained. The from-through construction restricts each coordinate, without permitting fractions or adding negative values.

entries.source: The selected image is no longer in this assembly.
entries.note: Selected image remains singular and absence is restricted to this assembly. Contrastive now plus absence conveys the changed present state in this error context, without asserting file deletion or loss of all images.
The complete label expresses a precise location. sa gnas is broader than the alternative technical gnas sa but is comprehensible for position here; this is not a required terminology correction.

The target value of X is qualified by a from-left-edge counting clause and pixel units. The mi relative construction modifies the pixel expression and preserves the physical origin. No mirrored/right-side meaning is introduced.
The same complete label structure identifies Y and counts pixels from the top edge. mgo is used spatially in this technical context, not as start in the text-direction sense.

entries.target: གཟུགས་བརྙན་འདི་གི་གཡོན་མགོའི་ཟུར་འདི་ གྲུབ་འབྲས་ཀྱི་འབྲི་གཞི་ནང་བཞག X དང་ Y འདི་པིག་སེལ་གྱི་ཧྲིལ་གྲངས་ཨིནམ་དང་ 0 ལས་འགོ་བཙུགསཔ་ཨིན། གཟུགས་བརྙན་གཞན་ཚུ་ རང་རང་གི་ད་ལྟོའི་ས་གནས་ནང་རང་སྡོདཔ་ཨིན། ནཱ་ལུ་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཚུ་གཅིག་གི་ཐོག་ཁར་གཅིག་བཞག་ཆོག ཤུལ་ལས་ནང་འདྲེན་འབད་མི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཚུ་ ཧེ་མའི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཚུ་གི་ཐོག་ཁར་འབྲིཝ་ཨིན། བཞག་ཚར་མི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཆ་མཉམ་ཤོང་ནི་ལུ་ འབྲི་གཞི་རྒྱ་བསྐྱེད་འབདཝ་ཨིན། བཏོག་ཁུལ་དང་ཚད་ཚུ་མི་བསྒྱུར།
entries.note: All seven intended facts are recoverable, but source-assisted confidence in the whole composed Dzongkha paragraph remains insufficient for integration. In particular the nominal whole-pixel predication and compressed all-images-fit/canvas-does-expansion sentence should be reviewed together as target prose. This is a linguistic-confidence hold, not a claim that shong or rgya bskyed is wrong. Independent primary sources now clear those lexical senses.

entries.source: X and Y must be whole numbers from zero to 2147483647.
entries.target: X དང་ Y གཉིས་ཆ་ར་ 0 ལས་ 2147483647 ཚུན་གྱི་ཧྲིལ་གྲངས་ཨིན་དགོ།
entries.note: Both X and Y are constrained to integer values from 0 through 2147483647; the obligation predicate and numerical endpoints survive. The reading is a requirement, not a rounding instruction.

entries.source: The selected image is no longer in this assembly.
entries.note: The full sentence says that the selected image is now absent within this assembly. In the selection-error context this communicates no longer present; it neither claims the image file was deleted nor broadens absence to all images. Primary grammar confirms that now plus a negative state can express no longer when previous state is contextual.

bo.source_clause: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas.
bo.independent_note: The command locates the image corner, not the whole image centre; output is rendered as result.

bo.source_clause: X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero.
bo.independent_note: Whole-number pixel quantities and zero origin are explicit.

bo.source_clause: Other images keep their current positions.
bo.independent_note: Each other image retains its current location.

bo.source_clause: images imported later are drawn on top.
bo.independent_note: Later import modifies the image group; drawn over earlier images is z-order, not a top-coordinate instruction.

bo.source_clause: The canvas expands to include all placed images.
bo.independent_note: All already-placed images must fit; the canvas becomes larger, and image scaling is not requested.
Crop regions and dimensions are both unchanged.

dz.source_clause: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas.
dz.independent_note: The top-left corner and result drawing surface are recoverable.

dz.source_clause: X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero.
dz.independent_note: Integer/pixel/0 intent is clear, but the complete nominal predication needs focused language-form review.

dz.source_clause: Other images keep their current positions.
dz.independent_note: Other images stay at their own current places.
The periphrasis permits one image on top of another.

dz.source_clause: images imported later are drawn on top.
dz.independent_note: Later imports are drawn over earlier images; no reordering of X/Y is implied.

dz.source_clause: The canvas expands to include all placed images.
dz.independent_note: All placed images fitting and canvas expansion are recoverable; the entire compressed purpose/subject/predicate construction remains held.
Both crop regions and sizes have a negative-change predicate.

changes: Make X/Y pixel counts explicit, retaining the integer restriction and zero.
Expand the purposive phrase and make the canvas size the expansion object.
Add explicit sentence punctuation after the two g-final command/permission clauses.
replacement_candidates.backtranslation: Place this image’s top-left corner on the output/result drawing surface. X and Y are pixel counts, in whole numbers starting at 0. Other images stay in their current positions. Here images can be placed one over another; later-imported images are drawn over earlier images. The canvas size is expanded so that every placed image fits. Crop regions and sizes do not change.

source_reliability_findings: DCT text extraction maps Tibetan stacks to unrelated scripts and displaces vowel marks. No damaged spelling was treated as verified; page-image attempts failed.
Physical Dzongkha fit/capacity is verified by an independent primary grammar, not inferred from Tibetan or from capacity noun alone.
Spatial expansion, pixel and integer are independently corroborated in HTML technical documentation. These lexical confirmations do not by themselves clear the held full help value.
The no-longer interpretation is a context-sensitive temporal reading of now plus negated state. The grammar provides an analogous complete example, not a mechanical dictionary equivalent.
The TUFS Dzongkha Expressions PDF also had broken extraction and failed screenshot retrieval; it was not used for spelling or full-sentence acceptance.
No claim of native-speaker certification, exact-phrase attestation, or Android font/rendering validation is made.
integration_rule: Only accept entries with decision=accept and matching target_sha256. The Dzongkha help and its full replacement candidate are not approved for integration until another full-value language review clears one exact hash.
